title: How to organise the hand tool wall and cabinets | Garage
description:
Keeps the tools you reach for weekly visible, findable, and provably all present.

This is the Hand Tool Wall and Cabinets in the Garage. About 60-90 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
Every hand tool hanging on its own drawn outline with no blank silhouettes, one hammer and one adjustable wrench at chest height nearest the door, saw teeth sheathed, and the cabinet latched.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Pull every hammer, screwdriver, plier, and wrench onto one sheet on the floor and count the duplicates honestl
Straighten: Hang by how often your hand reaches, not by tool family.
Shine: Wipe each tool with an oiled rag as it goes back up, and wipe the pegboard behind it.
Safety: Handsaws and chisels get a sheath or a blade guard before they touch the wall.
Standardize: Trace the silhouette of every tool onto the board in marker or paint.
Sustain: The driver goes back on its outline before you fold the step ladder away, not at the weekend.

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
Every hand tool has a drawn outline, and a blank outline means you find that tool before you close up.
